messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: Error help
parts:
Dear Brett,

I think that the reason is that there could have multiple measurement for certain run and certain feature. When I worked with maxquant data, I found that there are several measurements in certain run and certain feature. However, MSstats assume that there is only one measurement in certain run and certain feature. MSstats.daily v3.0.1 at msstats.org has new function for transforming MaxQuant output to MSstats input format. This function takes care of this issue. (use highest or mean measurement in certain run and certain feature, if there are multiple measurements). I hope this function can solve this issue. If you still had this error, please let me know.

- Meena

messages.author: 994731d36eeef20c
messages.subject: Re: Error help
parts:
Hi Brett,
Assuming that your problem is what Meena suggests, i.e. multiple measurements for a given feature in a single run, I guess you are using the evidence.txt table. Particularly, I have been using the peptide.txt table instead of evidence.txt. As you may know, peptide table aggregates all charge states, thus you should have a single for each peptide sequence. In R, you will have to 'melt' the peptide table though. And then, you just create the columns PrecursorCharge, FragmentIon, ProductCharge, and IsotopeLabelType.
  
If you still want to use the evidence.txt table, then I would use the "Modified.sequence" column as PeptideSequence and the "Charge" column as PrecursorCharge. If your data comes from a single LC-MS/MS analysis, then the combination of Modified.sequence and Charge should be unique, AFAIK. However, if you have multiple fractions then as Meena suggests you are likely to have multiple repeated features. In this case, you have 3 options: (1) use "aggregate" function of R to aggregate these multiple features (I use 'sum' for it); (2) use "paste" function to concatenate "Modified.sequence" with "Fraction"; and (3) use the column "Fraction" as it was the column ProductCharge (I never tried, but I guess it would work). 

Best,
Alex
